glosses: erwerben, besonders auf eine Weise, die kein Angebot mehr für andere Interessenten übriglässt

examples.text: Die Norweger haben alle am Markt angebotenen Grundstücke sofort weggekauft.
„Wenn eine Bank mich beauftragt, den Industriestaubsauger in einer Aktie anzumachen, sprich, alles, was in diesem Wert im Markt erhältlich ist, wegzukaufen, dann steigt diese Aktie natürlich extrem.“

translations.source_sense_description: die letzten Exemplare einer Ware kaufen
die letzten Exemplare einer Ware kaufen

glosses: To pay off, convince to refrain etc. by corrupt payment or other service.

examples.text: Then, Sir, as to Bribery and Corruption at Elections ... every Elector has a natural Byass to vote for one Man rather than another, and every Elector will vote according to his natural Byass, if he is not bought off: whoever endeavours to buy him off, must certainly come up to his Price, and this Price will be higher or lower, according to the Elector's Honour and Circumstances, and the natural Byass he has for the other Candidate. A great many Men may be perhaps bought off with 100 or 1000 Guineas, who, if half that sum were offered, would spurn it away with an honest Disdain.

You like to hear about gold.
A king filled his prison room
As full as the room could hold
To the top of his reach on the wall
With every known shape of the stuff.
’Twas to buy himself off his doom.

glosses: To gain release for (a person) from military service by payment of money.
